key_insight: EvoSteer turns multi-agent orchestration into an online, self-repairing process by using reference-anchored credit assignment to decide how each action should be evaluated and evolved during execution.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for building adaptive agentic systems that can update tool-using workflows on the fly instead of waiting until a failed run finishes.
method: Online self-evolving graph orchestration with step-level repair from execution features and learned value estimates.
Anchored Trajectory Balance (AnchorTB) to assign action coefficients by balancing subtrajectories against a frozen reference.
Validated Skill Admission to trial candidates first and promote only skills that pass a sequential evidence test under a shared budget.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on twelve datasets, with gains across question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and interactive decision making.
watch_item: The online admission and repair mechanism adds algorithmic complexity, so calibration of the sequential test and stability of the learned flow will likely be important in practice.
paper_title: EvoSteer: Online Self-Evolving Graph Orchestration via Reference-Anchored Credit Assignment
